title: Run to the End of a Tape Word
statement: Let $P$ be a register program with oracle, let $r$ be a work-tape register, and let $c_R$ and $n_x$ be states. Suppose that at state $c_R$ the transition function always prescribes the specified action that scans register $r$ to the end of its word and enters state $n_x$, regardless of the scanned input and work-tape symbols, and that $c_R$ is not a call state. For any initial configuration $c$, word $w$, and integers $n,p$ with $|w|-p=n$ and $0\le p$, after $n+1$ steps from the configuration with register $r$ containing $w$ and its head at $p$, the program is in state $n_x$ with that head at $|w|-1$; at every earlier time $t<n+1$, the configuration still has state $c_R$, contains the same word on register $r$, and its head is at some $q$ with $p\le q\le |w|$.
hypotheses_covered: The transition at state $c_R$ equals the specified end-scanning action for every input symbol and tuple of work-tape symbols
State $c_R$ is not a call state
$c$ is a configuration and $w$ is a Boolean word
$n$ is a natural number and $p$ is an integer
